newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO MOVE AGAINST MORE AILING BANKS - PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO MOVE AGAINST MORE AILING BANKS - PAPERS.

text.p: Bulgarian newspapers reported on Monday that up to 14 local banks might be closed or placed under special supervision as part of the government's efforts to stabilise the heavily indebted financial system.
However officials declined to comment on the news reports and denied media speculation that they had agreed a final list of names at a closed-door session late on Sunday.
The financial weekly Kapital said around 10 banks "definitely needed to be closed" and several more would require a precise assessment of their long-term prospects.

"The 10 or so worst banks are those which generate problems in the banking system -- illiquidity, blocking of settlement payments, lack of provisions, huge bad loans and chronic losses," the paper said.

Finance minister Dimitar Kostov said the issue of bank closures was not on the agenda of Sunday's meeting, which brought together cabinet ministers, ruling Socialist Party deputies and regional governors.
However a list of the banks to be closed or merged was circulated in Monday's newspapers and an official announcement could be expected in the coming weeks.

The government, battling an economic crisis, is under pressure from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to speed up structural reforms in the banking sector as a crucial element of a funding programme agreed in July.
The IMF postponed a second $115 million tranche this month due to Bulgaria's failure to close down scores of loss-making state firms and several insolvent banks.
The central bank has already initiated bankruptcy procedures against five banks.
This month the Sofia city court is expected to rule on insolvency suits against First Private Bank, the country's biggest private bank, and state-owned Mineralbank.
